episode.title: Restore resumed sessions through the canonical persisted runtime route
episode.before: At parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe, the desktop/TUI resume reader extracted provider, base_url, and api_mode only from top-level model_config keys, then fell back to billing_provider. It did not read model_config.gateway_runtime, even though gateway turns persisted their latest actual provider route there and CLI resume already consumed it through SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime. Consequently, a session whose provider changed through the messaging gateway could resume with its current stored model combined with a stale first-call billing provider or stale top-level route. The shared reader also returned any nonempty top-level route before consulting billing_provider, so delegating to it without adjustment would lose the established fallback that fills a missing top-level provider.
episode.after: At 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480, the desktop/TUI resume reader delegates provider, base_url, and api_mode recovery to SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime. That canonical reader prioritizes a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime, then top-level route fields, and uses a routable billing_provider only to fill a missing provider without overwriting explicit top-level data. CLI and desktop/TUI resume therefore interpret persisted route precedence consistently while retaining bare-billing-bucket filtering and legacy fallback behavior.
episode.diff: The change removes the desktop/TUI reader's duplicated top-level-field and billing-provider resolution, replacing it with a call to the shared session route reader. The shared reader changes billing fallback from a separate last-choice return into setdefault on the accumulated top-level route, preserving top-level endpoint/interface fields while filling only a missing provider. Two regression tests cover a nested latest route conflicting respectively with a frozen billing provider and stale top-level route fields. The focused test file passes 4/4 at the implementation ref; when the two new tests are copied to the parent, those two fail with stale 'anthropic' routing while the two pre-existing cases pass.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480 has parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe and changes hermes_state_gateway.py, tui_gateway/server.py, and tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py to fix resume route selection.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json fields resolved_commit, parent_commit, commit_show_stat, and changed_files_name_status; corroborated by git show --stat 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, _stored_session_runtime_overrides read provider, base_url, and api_mode directly from top-level model_config and fell back to model_config or row billing_provider, never consulting nested gateway_runtime.

The desktop/TUI reader now calls SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime(row) and derives provider, base_url, and api_mode from its returned route, removing its duplicate billing-provider filtering and top-level route reader.
The canonical session route reader gives a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime priority over top-level route keys and filters None values from that nested route.

The shared reader was adjusted so a routable billing_provider fills only a missing provider in the accumulated top-level route via setdefault; explicit top-level provider and endpoint/interface fields remain intact, while bare billing buckets remain excluded.
Gateway turns persist the actual model runtime under model_config.gateway_runtime, including provider, base_url, api_mode, and fallback status.
CLI resume already resolves stored routing through SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime, establishing that reader as the shared route interpretation boundary.
Deferred, cold, and eager desktop/TUI session-resume paths all consume _stored_session_runtime_overrides, so adapting that function affects the principal resume modes without changing each caller.

The added tests assert that desktop/TUI resume chooses nested gateway_runtime over both a stale first-call billing_provider and stale top-level provider/endpoint keys; one case also confirms CLI stored_session_route produces the same provider/interface tuple.
At the pinned implementation ref, all four tests in tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py pass.

evidence_units.claim: The implementation ref passes the focused regression file together with the shared reader's CLI resume tests, covering nested precedence, top-level fallback, invalid data, billing-provider fallback, bare-bucket exclusion, and explicit-provider precedence.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-partial-persisted-route-with-provider-fallback
candidate_atomics.description: Preserve explicit persisted endpoint/interface fields while filling only an absent provider from a routable legacy billing identity.

semantic_action.intent: Keep legacy or partially populated persisted routes resumable without allowing stale fallback metadata to replace explicit route fields.
semantic_action.pre_state: A session row may contain top-level endpoint or interface fields without a provider, plus a billing provider that may be either routable or only a non-routable aggregate bucket.
semantic_action.post_state: The resolved top-level route retains its explicit fields, gains the routable billing provider only when provider is absent, and ignores non-routable aggregate buckets.
semantic_action.validation: Shared route-reader tests verify routable billing fallback, bare-bucket exclusion, and explicit-provider precedence; the combined related suite passes 28 tests.

candidate_atomics.name: adapt-resume-consumer-to-canonical-route-reader
candidate_atomics.description: Replace a consumer-specific reconstruction of provider routing with the shared precedence-aware persisted-route resolver.

semantic_action.intent: Make all session resume interfaces select the same latest persisted provider route and avoid recombining a stored model with stale provider metadata.
semantic_action.pre_state: One resume interface reconstructs routing from top-level configuration and billing metadata, while the producer writes the latest actual route to a nested runtime field and another resume interface already reads it through a shared resolver.
semantic_action.post_state: The resume adapter obtains provider, endpoint, and interface mode from the shared resolver, so nested latest-runtime precedence and fallback semantics are consistent across resume interfaces.
semantic_action.validation: Regression tests compare desktop/TUI output with CLI route output and exercise conflicts between nested runtime, billing metadata, and top-level fields.

candidate_atomics.name: validate-conflicting-route-precedence
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise resume behavior with deliberately conflicting persisted representations and confirm that the latest nested runtime route wins.

semantic_action.intent: Prove that the adaptation removes the stale-provider failure rather than merely refactoring route-reading code.
semantic_action.pre_state: Test rows contain the same stored model but conflicting nested runtime, first-call billing provider, or stale top-level provider and endpoint fields.
semantic_action.post_state: Desktop/TUI and CLI resume resolve the nested provider and interface mode; the tests fail on the parent behavior and pass on the implementation ref.
semantic_action.validation: The focused file is green 4/4 at the implementation ref; the two new cases are red on the parent with the exact stale-provider tuple; the broader related suite is green 28/28.

candidate_workflows.name: unify-resume-routing-around-the-latest-persisted-runtime
candidate_workflows.description: When different interfaces persist or resume the same session route through different representations, establish one precedence-aware resolver, preserve necessary compatibility fallback, adapt divergent consumers to it, and verify conflicts red-on-base and green-on-change.

workflow_graph.goal: Resume a session on the provider endpoint and protocol most recently used by the session, consistently across user interfaces.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A producer persists the latest runtime route in one representation, but at least one resume consumer reads older or fallback representations with different precedence, allowing stale provider metadata to be paired with the stored model.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Resume consumers share a precedence-aware persisted-route resolver; explicit route fields and safe legacy fallback remain compatible; conflicting-state regression tests fail on the parent and pass on the implementation.
unresolved_or_deferred: The repository evidence validates resolved route tuples but does not execute a live external provider request or independently reproduce the reported HTTP 404.
No PR body, review discussion, or status-check metadata was available in the GitHub evidence bundle, so intent beyond the commit message and code/test behavior is not asserted.

unresolved_questions: Whether every historical persisted model_config shape is covered by the inspected tests is unknown; the evidence establishes the documented nested, top-level, invalid-data, billing-fallback, and bare-bucket cases.

The production 404 consequence described by the commit message was not independently exercised against an external provider; the local oracle proves the incorrect versus corrected provider/base_url/api_mode selection.
